claim: Seven years before the construction of the Brewer Fieldhouse in Columbia, Missouri, Chester Brewer worked as head football coach and head basketball coach of University Farm.
evidencia:
Page: Brewer Fieldhouse. Sentence: The Brewer Fieldhouse was a multi-purpose arena located in Columbia, Missouri, and home to the University of Missouri Tigers basketball team prior to the Hearnes Center opening in 1972.
Page: Brewer Fieldhouse. Sentence: Named after Chester Brewer, the building opened in 1929 to expand on the existing 500 seat Rothwell Gymnasium.
Page: Chester Brewer. Sentence: He served as the head football coach at Albion College (1899–1902), Michigan Agricultural College, now Michigan State University, (1903–1910, 1917, 1919), the University of Missouri (1911–1913), and the University Farm, now the University of California, Davis, (1922), compiling a career record of 97–51–4.
Page: Chester Brewer. Sentence: Brewer was also the head basketball coach at Michigan Agricultural (1903–1910), Missouri (1910–1911) and the University Farm (1922–1923), tallying a mark of 84–36, and the head baseball coach at Michigan Agricultural (1904–1910, 1918–1920) and Missouri (1911, 1914–1917, 1933–1934), amassing a record of 148–93–4.

Facts:
- Chester Brewer served as head football coach at Albion College from 1899 to 1902.
- Chester Brewer served as head football coach at Michigan Agricultural College, now Michigan State University, from 1903 to 1910, and again in 1917 and 1919.
- Chester Brewer served as head basketball coach at Michigan Agricultural College from 1903 to 1910.
- Chester Brewer served as head baseball coach at Michigan Agricultural College from 1904 to 1910 and again from 1918 to 1920.
- Chester Brewer served as head basketball coach at the University of Missouri from 1910 to 1911.
- Chester Brewer served as head football coach at the University of Missouri from 1911 to 1913.
- Chester Brewer served as head baseball coach at the University of Missouri in 1911, from 1914 to 1917, and from 1933 to 1934.
- Chester Brewer served as head football coach at University Farm, now the University of California, Davis, in 1922.
- Chester Brewer served as head basketball coach at University Farm from 1922 to 1923.
- Brewer Fieldhouse was named after Chester Brewer and opened in 1929 to expand the existing 500-seat Rothwell Gymnasium.
- Chester Brewer compiled a career football coaching record of 97–51–4, a basketball coaching record of 84–36, and a baseball coaching record of 148–93–4.
- Brewer Fieldhouse was a multi-purpose arena in Columbia, Missouri, and it was home to the University of Missouri Tigers basketball team until the Hearnes Center opened in 1972.
